message.content:
**Most Famous American Composers (by era & genre)**  

| Era / Genre | Composer | Why They’re Famous |
|-------------|----------|--------------------|
| **Early 19th c.** | **Stephen Foster** | “Oh! Susanna,” “Camptown Races” – the “father of American popular music.” |
| | **John Philip Sousa** | “The Stars and Stripes Forever” – the “march king.” |
| **Late 19th c. – Early 20th c.** | **Charles Ives** | Experimental modernist; “The Unanswered Question.” |
| | **George Gershwin** | Blended jazz & classical; “Rhapsody in Blue,” “An American in Paris.” |
| | **Aaron Copland** | “Appalachian Spring,” “Rodeo” – the “American sound.” |
| | **Samuel Barber** | “Adagio for Strings,” “Knoxville: Summer of 1915.” |
| | **Leonard Bernstein** | “West Side Story,” “On the Town” – Broadway & symphonic crossover. |
| **Mid‑20th c.** | **Philip Glass** | Minimalist pioneer; “Glassworks,” “Einstein on the Beach.” |
| | **John Adams** | Post‑minimalist; “Shaker Loops,” “Nixon in China.” |
| | **Steve Reich** | Minimalist; “Music for 18 Musicians,” “Different Trains.” |
| | **William Grant Still** | “Afro‑American Symphony” – first major symphony by an African‑American composer. |
| | **John Cage** | Avant‑garde; “4′33″,” prepared piano. |
| **Late 20th c. – Early 21st c.** | **John Williams** | Film scores: “Star Wars,” “Indiana Jones,” “Jurassic Park.” |
| | **Hans Zimmer** (German‑born, U.S.‑based) | “Inception,” “The Dark Knight,” “Interstellar.” |
| | **David Lang** | Pulitzer‑winning “The Little Match Girl’s Fire.” |
| | **Jennifer Higdon** | Pulitzer‑winning “Blue Cathedral.” |
| | **John Corigliano** | Pulitzer‑winning “The Ghosts of Versailles.” |
| **Contemporary & Diverse** | **Katherine Hoover** | Pulitzer‑winning “The Great American Songbook.” |
| | **Terry Riley** | Minimalist; “In C.” |
| | **Mason Bates** | “The Last Airbender” soundtrack; blends electronic & orchestral. |
| | **Julián Carrillo** | “Sonido” – experimental; “The Sound of the Future.” |

> **Why “most famous” is subjective**  
>  * Popularity varies by audience (classical vs. film vs. jazz).  
>  * Some composers are household names (e.g., John Williams), while others are revered in academic circles (e.g., Charles Ives).  
>  * The list above mixes composers who have shaped American music across multiple genres and eras.

**Quick Takeaway**  
- **John Williams** and **George Gershwin** are probably the most recognizable to the general public.  
- **Aaron Copland**, **Leonard Bernstein**, and **Philip Glass** are pillars of American classical music.  
- **John Cage** and **Charles Ives** pushed the boundaries of what music could be.  
- Contemporary composers like **Jennifer Higdon** and **John Corigliano** continue to win major awards and shape the future of American composition.
